$comment: P69 (lane `cs`, D-LIR-GUARDED-RANGE-DOES-NOT-COVER-BLOCKS-THE-LOWERING-CREATES): THE CREATED BLOCK AN ORDINARY C PROGRAM PUTS IN A GUARDED BODY. `a && b` and `a || b` are lowered to a two-way branch feeding a phi at the join, with no promotion pass involved, and the edge that skips the right operand is split in a block the lowering creates, laid out after every block of the function. Inside a `__try` that block belongs to the guarded body, and since a guarded region is a set of contiguous runs it has a scope record of its own, with the region's filter and handler. The sibling examples/c/seh_asm_goto_output_stored_on_its_edges_is_guarded shows the same mechanism where the created block STORES; this one shows the shape no reference lacks and every program has. Exit bits by return value: 1-4 `&&` as a condition with the operand null, non-zero and zero (the short-circuit edge taken and not), 5 a fault IN the operator reaches the handler with `t` unwritten, 6 a fault AFTER the operator reaches it with the `t` the short-circuit edge stored, 7-9 `||` as a value and a fault in it, 10 the operator two regions deep with an inner filter that declines (the outer handler runs), 11 the same unfaulted.

$commentHostCoverage: WHAT EACH HOST ASSERTS OF THIS FILE (the two runners' behaviour as examples/c/declspec_requests_are_honoured_on_pe states it from their sources). On a WINDOWS host both corpus runners compile the pe pair and RUN the image, debug and release: the exit code is read there and only there. On a host that is NOT Windows the in-process runner (tests/examples) still COMPILES the baseline arm for the pe pair — a refusal of this file is caught there — and then stops at `runOn`: it spawns nothing, so the exit code is NOT read, and the release arm is not compiled. The CLI-subprocess runner (integrated_tests) binds one host-runnable target per manifest, so off Windows it never compiles this file at all. What the image DOES when a fault is raised is therefore read on Windows alone, by this example; that the created block HAS its record is read on every host by the unit claims named next.
$commentRedOnDisable: WRITTEN, NOT READ — no mutation named here has been built and read, and this example is a corpus check, never a pin. The claims every host runs are `GuardedRegionRuns.AShortCircuitInAGuardedBodyIsSplitInARunItsHandlerNeverReads` in tests/lir/test_guarded_region_runs.cpp (the records by block, and the register the split writes) and `Program_CompileFiles.AGuardedShortCircuitsEdgeSplitIsUnderAScopeRecordOfItsOwn` in tests/program/test_compile_pipeline.cpp (the produced image's scope table). The mutations are arms of tests/mutations/arms.registry (`lir-no-run-is-emitted_guarded-region-runs`, `lir-no-run-is-emitted_compile-pipeline`, `lir-a-phi-edges-split-is-created-around-the-creator`): each READ `passed` in the sweep of checkpoint 14 (macos-arm64-debug, run 20261012-151311-82d3dd43) against the cases of that day, and none has been read against these two claims, which are younger than that sweep. A PREDICTION from the code, for this example alone: with no run emitted the split block is outside every range, and since that block holds a register copy and a jump — nothing that reads memory — this program would still exit 42; the example shows the shape COMPILES and RUNS right, and it is the unit claims that show the record is there.
